en: Maṇicūḍa-parivarta-stotra:
Siri siddhārtha svāhā || 1 || Siri siddhārtha svāhā || 2 || Buddha-siri svāhā || 3 || Siri || 4 ||
The Ritual Praise of the Ever-Flourishing Tree: Adorned with myriad jewels, it is wondrous beyond compare;
Its substance extends throughout and fills the world. With leaves of salvation and flowers of [virtue], it pervades all;
All Buddhas emerge from amidst its blossoms, And all wisdom arises from within its fruit.

Able to nourish the five kinds of sons of light, Able to subdue the five kinds of greedy and deluded minds, The King of Mind is pure and ever-vigilant; For those with faith and realization, it increases mindfulness and recollection.
For those who advance with firm resolve, It leads them onto the level and correct path.
Now, having been granted the eye of Buddha-nature, I am able to behold the wondrous Dharma-body in its four aspects;
Furthermore, having been granted the ear of Buddha-nature, I am able to hear the three eternally pure [realms].
Therefore, with a tranquil mind, I pay homage and offer praise—these are words of truth that eliminate all distracted thoughts.
Inadvertently committing various transgressions in the past, I now repent with earnestness so that my sins may be extinguished.
May the precious trees of eternal prosperity flourish within the ocean of my life. Be compassionate and hear my true confession;
there are infinite names according to various lands, and infinite musical arts according to various lands.
Father of Compassion, the nature of all luminosity; Mother of Pity, who rescues all who are plundered— Now deliver me from the jackals and wolves! You are this light, the peerless great sage;
From you comes an inexhaustible treasury, Filled with every kind of precious jewel.
He who bestows gifts upon all the destitute, Granting each their heart's desire according to their wish—
this Great Sage is the second honored one. Furthermore, he is the third, the capable translator,
Together with his pure retinue, Who proclaims the holy intent so that all may awaken.
Furthermore, this is the eighth mark of radiance: the fundamental characteristic of all Buddhas, the refuge and support for those who seek guidance;
the sovereign king within the hearts of all wisdoms, adorned with every jewel, the truly awakened one, and the gateway to liberation for all who perform virtuous deeds.
To those who plunder, he provides protection; to those in bondage, he brings liberation;
to those oppressed, he grants relief and ease. To those afflicted by afflictions, he brings joy and consolation;
he heals all who uphold filial piety and causes all to revive their luminous nature.

I now earnestly and piteously beseech you all: May we leave this physical body—a sea of poisonous fire with surging waves that never ceases— Where Māra exhausts himself entering and exiting, swallowing ships and galleys;
Which is originally a rākṣasa kingdom, the palace of Māra, And further, a dense forest, a marsh of reeds and rushes.
Various evil birds and beasts run crosswise; A gathering place for venomous insects, vipers, and adders—
These too are the bodies of the Mara of greed through evil karma, And further, many forms of base and wretched existence,
As well as the five-layered pits of the realm of darkness, And the court of the five poisons of ignorance.
It is also the sprout of the three poisons of lack of compassion, And further, the spring of the five poisons of lack of wisdom;
The two wheels of cold and heat, upper and lower, The two sets of seven, these twelve palaces—
All male and female māras arise Manifesting from the conditions of the physical body.
Furthermore, it is the gateway to the three realms and five destinies;
It is also the mouth of all māras throughout the ten directions and the dark mother of all māra-kings.
It is the root source of all evil karma, And the heart of the fierce and venomous yakṣas; It is also the thought within the mind of the Māra of Greed.
The armor and weapons of all Māras, The poisonous net of all who violate the teachings,
That which can sink treasures and merchants, That which can obscure the light of the sun and moon—
O Buddha, All the gateways to the hells, And all the paths of saṃsāra.
Though you are but a phantom, you dwell eternally in the King of Nirvana; yet now you have been utterly consumed by fire and imprisoned in a perpetual dungeon.
You have returned to create obstacles for me, binding me with shackles and fetters that constantly entwine me.
This has driven me to madness and intoxication, leading me to violate the three constants and the four bases of existence.
The great earth, grasses, trees, stars, and constellations; The dust of the earth, grains of sand, and fine rain—
May the transgressions and faults I have committed, Which are many times more than these by tens of millions,
Be seen by the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, Who, arising in great compassion, grant me absolution from my sins.
Listen to these words of my bitter suffering; lead me away from this sea of poisonous fire.
Grant me the water of liberation, fragrant with the scent of precepts, to wash the twelve-jeweled crown, robes, and ornaments from my wondrous nature so that it is free of dust.
Adorn my pure body and make it upright and beautiful.
May the three poisons and the knots of the three winters be removed; May the six thieves and the winds of the six poisons be quelled.
May the Great Dharma descend like spring to cause the ground of nature to flourish, And may the flowers and fruits of the tree of nature grow lush and abundant.
May the great waves of the ocean of fire be stilled, Along with the dark clouds, mists, and all entanglements and coverings.
When the Great Dharma descends, its universal radiance shines forth; may my mind-nature remain ever luminous and pure.
I pray that the maladies of ignorance and delusion accumulated over many kalpas, as well as all malevolent spirits, demons, and ghosts, may be eliminated.
May the medicine of the Great Dharma swiftly heal me, and through the power of divine mantras, may these afflictions be bound and driven away.
I am beset by such numerous obstacles, And further burdened by countless hardships.
Great Sage, behold me with your own compassion; Rescue me and do not let these calamities and afflictions remain.
I pray that you will send down your mercy, And release me from the bonds of demons and malevolent spirits.
Now dwelling in the pit of fire, quickly lead them to rest in the pure land;
The Great Physician-King for all who are ill, the Great Radiance for all who are in darkness;
Diligently gathering those who are scattered in the four directions, causing the hearts of the devas to rejoice.
I now pray that you revive me from death; I now pray that you illuminate me from this darkness.

May the Māra King disperse throughout the ten directions; do not lead me along, staining me within the three realms of existence, leaving me dazed and unconscious, so that I commit offenses against the three constants and the four bases of the body.

Ignorance, delusion, and craving constantly flourish together; May the Great Sage swiftly extend his hands of compassion To apply the great medicine of the Dharma and bring healing, Pressing upon my crown— the luminous Buddha-nature—
To protect me at all times, And not allow the factions of Māra to come and cause me harm.
Rejoicing with me before my original realm, May the afflictions of my vast eons be exhausted;
May my luminous nature be adorned with wondrous splendor, Returning to its original state, no longer sinking into the realms of greed and desire,
And once again manifesting pure and wondrous radiance— A new, pure land adorned with myriad jewels.
The newly bestowed lapis lazuli blue sun shines upon my Dharma-body and pure, wondrous realm;
from this moment, O Great Sage, it is a time of auspiciousness. It universally illuminates the luminous nature of us all;
its wondrous color has no peer in the world, and its supernatural manifestations are likewise so.
Sometimes manifesting as a youth with subtle and wondrous marks, or appearing as the five kinds of female māras who cause insanity;
sometimes manifesting as a maiden with a dignified and beautiful body, or appearing as the five kinds of those who cause madness and confusion—
this is the Vidyārāja who pities his children, and this is the Vidyā-nature who can save his father.
You are the supreme elder brother of all Buddhas, And likewise the mother of wisdom and compassion;

With a sincere heart, I cry out in earnest lamentation. O true father, whose face is filled with loving-kindness, I pray you will pardon all the transgressions I have committed, And cause me to leave behind the deceptive intimacy of Māra’s house.
O Unsurpassed Vidyārāja, the Mightiest of the Mighty; Unsurpassed King of Wisdom, the Nectar of Immortality;

Universal Bestower of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel upon all beings— I call out with a sincere heart from this deep sea of fire, Beseeching you with earnest and piteous cries: Save us from suffering! To remain indifferent is shameful.
I pray that you may spread wide the wings of compassion, Causing me to leave behind all predatory demon-birds,
The ignorant physical body, and all kinsmen— All these children within the dark and deep pit,
Whose internal and external natures are filled with demons, Constantly harming my pure essence.
No evil beast can compare to you; how could any venomous snake be your equal?
Like the biting wind and frost at the end of autumn, they blow away all that is wholesome.
With earnest and piteous cries, I offer this sincere invocation to the Great Physician King, who possesses sublime deeds and wisdom.
The virtuous spiritual friend brings healing upon encounter; the one of excellent compassion meets with joy.
All bodily natures, whether obstructed or unobstructed, have long been wounded and submerged in the ocean of birth and death, their limbs and joints scattered throughout the three realms.
I pray that they may be gathered back together, ascend once more, and transcend all phenomenal existence.
Do not further sever the flow of the True Dharma; do not cast [it] into the mouths of the māras.
By the power of great skillful means and compassion, I entreat you, O Sūbhūti and all you vidyā-natures:
do not let yourselves be seized and carried off by the armies of māras; do not let yourselves be slain again by enemies.
With wings of radiant light and the covering of compassion, Abandoning me,
you rain down the nature of the body; I pray only that you lower the hand of great compassion,
Pressing upon my threefold pure Dharma-body to sweep away the fetters of kalpas, And bathe me of the dust and grime of kalpas past.
Open for me the luminous eye of the *dharmatā*, so that I may unimpededly behold the bodies in the four directions;
thus may I be freed from the four kinds of great suffering.
Open for me the luminous ear of the *dharmatā*, so that I may unimpededly hear the sounds of the sublime Dharma.
Unimpededly hearing the wondrous sound of the Dharma, One is thereby freed from the falsehoods and deviousness of the various stages of parinirvāṇa.
The mouth that opens forth the radiance of my *dharmatā* Extols the three constants and the four *dharmakāyas*.
Thus, one transcends the deluded mind that was previously muddled and confused.
Open the hand of the radiance of my *dharmatā*; Touching everywhere the fourfold body of tranquil suchness, I am thus freed from the calamity of sinking into the four great elements;
My many years of fetters are fully loosened, And I attain the ability to tread the path of the three eternal True Dharmas.
May I tread the path of the Three Constant True Dharmas And swiftly arrive at the Land of Peace and Bliss.
May I restore my original *tathatā*-mind, Pure radiance ever intermingled with tranquility;
Pure radiance ever intermingled with tranquility, Forever free from delusion and all perversions.
May I always behold my compassionate Father, and never again suffer the pains of saṃsāra;
May my faculties be purified and my mind awakened, and never again be muddled or ignorant and lacking in realization;
Now that I rely upon the Great Holy One, may I never again sink into the path of birth and death.
Swiftly lower your hands of compassion and light; do not cast us aside.
With a heart of sincere lamentation and fervent supplication, I entreat you:
May you descend with great compassion to constantly shield and protect me, And forgive my transgressions throughout kalpas as vast as space, Just as you did for those men and women of the past.
I am the lamb of the Great Sage’s Radiance; With tears and sobs, I lament my grievous injustice.
Suddenly seized by jackals, wolves, and fierce beasts, I have been snatched away from the pasture of virtuous light.
I pray that you, O Great Compassionate One, will take me in, And release me into the flock of gentle radiance.
Having attained the mountain forest of the sublime and majestic Dharma, you wander with sovereign ease, ever free from fear.

Furthermore, you are the seed of the Great Sage’s bright grain; though cast into the midst of a dense thicket of thorns, I pray that you extend great compassion to gather and harvest it, bringing it together toward the luminous granary of the Dharma assembly.
Furthermore, this great sage’s grapevine, Originally planted in the pure garden of the Dharma, Is now completely entwined by the creeping vines of the Qieluo;
It draws upon my wondrous power, causing it to wither and fade.
Furthermore, this great sage’s fertile soil Has been overrun by Māra, who plants trees of the five poisons.
I only pray for the sharp blade of the Dharma’s hoe to cut down, burn,
and clear away all other evil weeds and thorns; may the fire of the precepts utterly eliminate them,
so that the fifteen kinds of flourishing sprouts may be fully extended and the fifteen [virtues] brought to fruition.
Furthermore, this is the new and wondrous robe of the Great Sage; Suddenly it has been defiled by the dust of Māra.
I only pray for the water of the Dharma to wash it clean and brighten it; May I obtain the pure body of the Dharmakāya.
With earnest and piteous cries, I entreat with a sincere heart: May the Tree of Life, adorned with myriad jewels, [be restored].
Supreme, peerless, and wondrous King of Physicians, Peaceful, pure in karma, and endowed with all virtues,
Ever-flourishing jewel-tree within the ocean of life, With a foundation as firm as the vajra-body,
Your trunk is truth and free from falsehood; Your branches are vast and long, eternally joyful.
Endowed with all jewels, its leaves are compassion; Its nectar-fruit is ever fresh and never withers.
Those who eat it forever sever the stream of birth and death; Its fragrant scent pervades the world.
Having attained the state of a Great Sage, one hopes for eternal life; It is the tree that can revive the Dharma-nature and perpetually flourish.
With wisdom pure and empty, ever vigilant, The King of Mind skillfully discerns;

with earnest, compassionate cries, I entreat you with a sincere heart: May the Dharma King, the Buddha Viśvabhū, grant that my physical body remain forever healthy and unharmed, And that my Buddha-nature be free from all entanglements and defilements.
At all times increasing mindfulness, Causing one to leave the mouths of all devouring māras, Forever separated from evil karma and greed,
May they be placed within the wondrous Dharma-forest of incense and flowers, And led into the pure flock of gentle lambs.
May the foundation of my faith be ever firm; may I attain entry into that which is worthy of praise.
With earnest, piteous wailing and a sincere heart, I entreat you:
O Compassionate Father, Dharma King, Lord of Life, may you rescue my nature from calamity and misfortune, and may you cause my pure body to be forever joyful.
You who bring vast tranquility and rescue from suffering, You who manifest compassion and abandon faults, grant me the luminous nature;
Grant me the pure body and act as my refuge.
You can destroy the mountains of blades and the forests of swords, And you can subdue lions, venomous serpents, and vipers.
All incurable diseases can be eliminated; Difficult-to-renounce attachments are made to part.
I now resolutely uphold the seal of the Dharma; The Great Sage, in his compassionate pity, constantly shields and protects me.
With earnest devotion, I chant the name of the Compassionate Father; May this ultimate and precious aspiration be fulfilled.
I address you, O assembly of omniscient ones: each of you listen to these words of truth regarding our livelihood.
The Dharma King Mañjuśrī, endowed with wisdom, appears as clearly as if before our very eyes.
Having now received the realization of the Great Sage, we must surely renounce all worldly attachments and cravings.
The Dharma Gate of Resolute Peace of Mind: Diligently seek nirvana to cross the great ocean.
Furthermore, tell those of high rank, merit, and virtue Who focus their intent on diligently seeking liberation:
Exert yourselves in refined cultivation without idleness; Swiftly depart from all fears of birth and death.
All worlds are impermanent; all dependencies are likewise not true.
Like the illusory city on the desert isle, the foolish rush toward them and lose their very lives.
Worldly splendor and noble rank are attained by those with little merit who possess mere mastery.
Like clouds surging upon the peaks of the four mountains, gathered together yet swiftly dispersed by the wind, this foul and impure physical body does not endure for long;
when the time of impermanence arrives, it is utterly destroyed.
Like the flowers and leaves of spring that briefly flourish upon their branches, how could they ever remain firm and eternally verdant?
When the physical body was fashioned by a skilled craftsman, it became a hollow and illusory abode for the evil Māra King;
having completed such a dwelling, he ensnares the luminous nature which remains hidden within.
Driven by a chain of insatiable hunger and devoid of gratitude, he ceaselessly slaughters sentient beings.
Though one spends the entire day devouring various parts of the body, one still cannot escape the suffering of birth and death;
though one accumulates all manner of wealth and treasures,
they all remain behind on the day of impermanence, serving only as shackles for the nature of clarity.
First sever ignorance, attachment, and desire; for those are the ocean of all afflictions.
In the future, they will become the conditions for receiving various calamities, and in the present life, they serve as shackles upon the Buddha-nature.
Alas! The multitudes of sentient beings in the world are unable to seek the true path with sincere faith.
Day and night they seek wealth without ceasing; all this is for the sake of the flesh-body, the lord of the demon of greed.
When the flesh-body is destroyed, the demon emerges. Their sinful karma brings calamity upon their pure nature, and wherever they are reborn, they suffer various misfortunes;
this is truly because the karma of their previous lives was not upright.
This cherished physical body must eventually be abandoned; for all that is born returns to extinction.
All wealth, treasures, fields, and houses—though one desires not to part with them, they will ultimately be left behind.
Even if one attains glory and splendor within this world, one must break the heart’s attachment and weary of the suffering of birth and death.
Abandoning pride and negligence, one should single-mindedly and diligently cultivate the path to Nirvāṇa.

At birth one is naked, and so too is one at death. Though men and women may amass many wives, concubines, and ornaments for the body, after death these remain for others to provide for different masters.
Standing alone and utterly ashamed of their concurrent evil karma, they must, after death, carry their burdens upon their backs before the King of Equality.
All are compelled by the principles of justice; they are cast back into the suffering of the cycle of birth and death, where they are once again ensnared by the Demon King.
Failing to encounter favorable conditions, they gradually become more defiled.
Some enter hell or are consumed by flames; some dwell together with various māras in eternal prisons, singing, dancing, and playing all manner of music;
they consume a hundred flavors and manage fields and houses—all is like a dream seen upon waking, whereupon it vanishes.
Contemplate this minutely: there is nothing upon which to rely.
In the conventional truth, all kinsmen and relatives are but temporary; how are they different from staying as guests in a lodging?
At evening, many people dwell together; at dawn, they part ways and return to their own lands.
Wives, concubines, sons, and daughters are like creditors, for all have caused mutual harm in past lives.
Furthermore, out of compassion for enemies and thieves, one should return their strength to them;

thus, the mind is divided to provide sustenance for those sentient beings who eat flesh. Their bodies are like graves, and moreover, they are no different from bottomless pits where countless classes of living beings are slain in vain, providing provisions for the armies of the three poisons and the six thieves.
The Buddha-nature is serene, yet it is confined within; Afflictions press upon it, causing constant suffering.
The fires of lust and hunger, along with past karmic retributions, Never for a single moment fail to boil it.
As the world gradually degenerates, there is perpetual haste and oppression; Above and below, one constrains the other, with no joy or delight.
Sentient beings suffer only increasing poverty and misery; The wealthy are driven by Māra and find no rest.
Those who cultivate goodness are extremely few, While those who commit evil are boundless.
The King of Lust, Greed, and the Blazing Mara, Even when encountering favorable conditions, causes them to retreat and scatter.
They constantly compete with flowery words face-to-face, Lacking all sense of shame or fear;
Toward the Sage’s radiant and powerful wisdom, They heap groundless and false speech.
Sentient beings are mostly shrouded by ignorance, And are unwilling to diligently cultivate the true path.
Slandering the Buddha, destroying the Dharma, and being arrogant toward the true Sangha— You who inflict harm and offer no protection, you wise ones, observe closely:
By whom were the great and small boundaries established?
At what time and for what conditions were they created? One must thoroughly understand these two aspects of harm and benefit.
The various forms and types of all sentient beings, the formation and destruction of worlds, and their locations—these are all secret matters.
You, Mañjuśrī, have fully revealed where all things ultimately return;
you have clearly explained all essential natures and characteristics.
You who seek liberation should awaken to and reflect deeply upon these truths:
practice generosity, observe the fasts, and diligently recite the scriptures; employ wisdom to discern and receive the pure precepts;
cultivate compassion, fear of wrongdoing, and a preference for proper conduct. By relying on the power of these factors, you shall escape calamity and distress.
Leaping with joy, firm and steadfast in the True Dharma, Diligently cultivating wisdom and dwelling according to the Dharma,
Together abandoning all improper conduct, With a resolute mind settled in the state of liberation,
Because of the nature of present mastery, One is able to relinquish all habitual tendencies of craving and desire.
Impermanence suddenly arrives and presses upon us; when that moment comes, what use is regret?
What can it avail? Reflect carefully upon this world below: there is not a single thing that can be relied upon.
Relatives, sons, daughters, wives, and concubines—on the day of impermanence, none shall take our place.
Only the rain-like karma of good and evil follows one wherever they go or sit, according to their Buddha-nature.
All worldly glory, wealth, and precious playthings must be abandoned on the day of impermanence;
therefore, let the wise observe this and practice in advance, so as not to be invaded by the King of Māra or the cycle of birth and death.
Able to relinquish all cherished attachments, honors, and pleasures, One is immediately freed from sinking into the three poisons and five desires.
May all universally vow to unite their minds and ascend the Path of Rightness, Swiftly attaining nirvāṇa and the pure land.
The seven calamities and four sufferings are fundamentally non-existent there; Therefore, it is called the Land of Constant Joy.
I universally invoke all the vidyādharas and the pure hosts of those possessing supernatural powers;
may each of you, out of the power of your compassionate mercy, take pity on me and forgive all my transgressions.
I address the Sovereign of the Ever-Luminous Luminous Realm, together with the five kinds of vast and magnanimous [Buddhas].
The King of Constant Abiding Jewel Light, In countless worlds and all their lands;
Furthermore, he opens the wondrous and extraordinary fragrance of space, With radiant, brilliant, and pure marks.
The ground of diamond jewels is truly worthy of praise, Adorned by the five kinds of awakened intentions.
I further prostrate to the Honored One who first manifested through transformation, the Mother of all Buddhas, the Dharmakāya endowed with the marks, and his father,
the eternally victorious Samantabhadra; as well as the joyful son of the five sciences,
and I also prostrate to the second messenger, Sukhāloka, and to the venerable one who fashioned the new form.
The valiant and sovereign Wind of Pure Dharma, along with the five classes of heroic sons; furthermore,
the three great men who are teachers of the Way, beginning with the second honored one, Vast and Tranquil Count,
together with him of Lightning Radiance, and the one of Serene and Profound Mutual Support.
I further invoke the Palace of Solar and Lunar Radiance, The abode where the Buddhas of the three times reside;
The seven and twelve great ship-captains, Along with all other hosts of radiant beings.
I further invoke the twelve subtle and wondrous seasons, Whose essence is auspicious, pure, and luminous.
He constantly manifests in male and female forms, Uniquely sublime and majestic, beyond compare.
Furthermore, he invokes the Buddhas of the five kinds of light:
The powers of water and fire, light, subtle wind, And pure breath with its gentle nature— All these are the supreme powers within the power of the Illuminator.
Furthermore, I pay homage to the Lord of the World, Abundant Wealth; to the Ten Heavenly Kings, heroic, powerful, and sovereign;
to the Magician who subdues Māra with great strength; to Kṣāntidhara and Jvalanāntaka;
and I further pay homage to Yamāntaka, the Benevolent Contemplator—this is the compassionate visualization of Yamarāja.
The King who truly adjudicates affairs with impartiality, together with the pure assembly of the Five Myrobalans; furthermore,
those who have opened the exceptionally supreme flower-crown, the auspicious and pure transmitters of the message,
the original manifestations of the Buddhas' forms, and those equal to the compassionate fathers of the three times.
Furthermore, I invoke the sounds of response and awakening, As well as the four clear divisions, the brothers, the three robes,
the three wheels, and the great donor; And those of life, body, grasses, and trees,
Again I invoke the forty powerful messengers, Along with the seven pillars of firm adornment.
Each celestial realm supported itself from within, Each manifesting the form of subduing Māra.
Furthermore, I invoke the Lord Mañjuśrī, The Sun of Awakening who illuminates the silent realm.
From that Great Radiance he came to this world, To propagate the True Dharma and save his virtuous sons.
The twelve great *mudrās* of the explanatory manual;
the seventy-two *vibhūṣaṇas* for those who receive the teaching at the Dharma Hall residence; the pure and virtuous assembly as well as the listeners;
furthermore, the twelve bodies of the new initiates; the twelve Radiant Kings (*Prabhāpāla*) and Huiming.
Possessing the five pure precepts of wholesome dharmas, The five kinds of wisdom, and the five-layered courtyard,
The ever-victorious robe of all Buddhas, Is the new *śrīvatsa* that rescues from suffering;
Its four purities are the winds of liberation, And it is the witness to the true Great Dharma.
Furthermore, I declare the characteristics within the assembly of wholesome dharmas: The upper and lower, the internal and external, serve as the basis for discerning all fundamental appearances;
From the highest to the middle and lowest realms, there is nowhere they do not pervade.
I further address all beings filling the void, And the hosts of powerful, reverent, and faithful deities.
And the sons of the gods from all the celestial realms who uphold the pure True Dharma;
furthermore, those who have set forth upon the noble path of virtuous karma, the masters of the three types of knowledge (*traividya*),
those with the true physical marks, the ever-victorious sons who save themselves and others, and those who firmly maintain the truth.
I further declare the luminous nature of liberation, the inexhaustible treasury at all times,
as well as that supreme primordial mind of the past, along with the other natures of merit and clarity;
I now truly believe in the new realm of clarity and those who dwell eternally therein.
I pray that each of you will descend with the power of compassion, Sheltering us and constantly observing us.
Now, with single-minded devotion, I seek the Noble Ones; May you swiftly grant me the fulfillment of my true aspirations.
May I be delivered from all calamities and misfortunes, And may all karmic obstacles and hindrances be utterly extinguished.
Homage to the pure and subtle wind, The primordial wisdom of the luminous Honored One’s heart.
Constantly dwelling and moving with perpetual mastery Within the palaces of light in the four directions,
Possessing pure radiance and great power of wisdom— I now praise you with a sincere and universal heart.
Compassionate Father, Clear-Sighted Son, Wind of Pure Dharma, Along with all the signs of wholesome dharmas,
All the Buddhas of universal radiance: May you each, out of compassion, accept my request,
Grant me the gate of liberation from suffering, And cause me to swiftly reach the realm of eternal light.
Again, he praised the assembly who cultivate the path through wholesome karma— those of the past, future, and present—
who each opened their pure mouths of ambrosia and uttered sounds of great compassion to relinquish my sins.
Having now practiced this verse of praise at the end of the night, how could I possibly exhaustively explain it according to the Dharma?
To the assembly of sages, ordinary beings, and all devas, we pray that no calamities befall us and that our transgressions be extinguished.
Furthermore, we invoke all the vidyādharas and the pure hosts endowed with supernatural powers;
may each descend with great compassion to provide universal shelter and protection, uprooting all our faults and misdeeds.
Pure Radiance Power-Wisdom, Compassionate Father, Bright Son, Pure Dharma-Wind,
Subtle Mark, Mindful Contemplation, Thought-Intent, Yishu (Iṣu), Lightning Radiance, Vast Mind;
again I beseech the True King of Equality, the Valiant Warrior, the New Yishu.
O heroic and sovereign Mañjuśrī, together with the assembly of pure luminous beings,
who embody the characteristics of all virtuous dharmas— may you universally assist us at all times and on every day through all meritorious deeds,
exerting diligent power so that our virtues may be swiftly accomplished according to our aspirations.
The following verse should be recited according to the Sanskrit original:
"Homage to Mañjuśrī, the King endowed with wisdom; From him emerges the wondrous jewel-flower of light, its stem extending through the world-systems;
Both its roots and its fruit, throughout his entire being, are worthy of praise."
If a person can eat this fruit, they will immediately attain a long-lived body that does not die;
or if they taste its nectar-like flavor, their inner and outer selves will be adorned, bringing joy to the mind.
Such a one becomes a place of reliance for all sentient beings, who, through being encouraged and sustained, shall find peace and firmness.
You are able to grant us that which is beyond arising and ceasing; how could we not join our hearts in praise?
We reverently prostrate to the one named Compassionate Father—supreme, ultimate, and wishing for suchness.
First is the Radiant Honored One; second is Wisdom; third is Ever-Victorious.
Fourth is joy; fifth is diligent cultivation; sixth is truthfulness;
seventh is faith; eighth is patience; ninth is rectitude of mind; tenth is merit;
eleventh is harmony through a unified mind.
Twelfth: Both Inner and Outer Radiance; Adorned with Perfect Wisdom like the Sun;
Named the Twelve Hours; Complete Merit. First Section:
First, the Unsurpassed King of Radiance; Second, the Buddha Mother of Excellent Wisdom.
Third is the Buddha Constantly Victorious in Forethought; Fourth is the Buddha Joyful in the Five Sciences;
Fifth is the Buddha Diligently Cultivating Delight in Knowledge; Sixth is the Buddha Truly Creating Marks;
Seventh is the Buddha Pure Wind of Faith; Eighth is the Buddha Sunlight of Forbearance.
Ninth is Ajitaraśmi; tenth is Jñānākaravarṇa Buddha; eleventh is Samāhitavajraprabha Buddha;
twelfth is Prajñābhāsa-vyūha-kāya Buddha, the King of the Dharma within the three periods of time, who reveals all secret matters.
The nature and characteristics of the two schools and the three times, All are clearly manifested by the wisdom of the Unsurpassed King of Radiance,
free from doubt or obstruction; Ever victorious, the source of joy in the five sciences,
with diligent mind creating forms that are eternally real, Faith and patience constantly illuminate.

One should mindfully recognize kindness and achieve meritorious virtue; with harmony and a unified mind, increase wisdom and clarity to the ultimate degree, remaining forever broad-minded and at ease.
To praise and extol the Buddhas of the four directions—this initial sound of praise, this initial sound of praise—is profound and subtle in its meaning.
It is fitting to follow the Brahma.
First Layer: *Ullambana-āpūrṇa*. May those who valorously protect the Dharma always bring clarity;
may the assembly be worthy of praise from the very beginning. We pray that you descend with great compassion to protect us.
The unsurpassed noble one, the radiant one, who covers this place with a multitude of lights;
the protector and the watchman, who is ever able to nourish the tender lambs;
the true judge, the holy one, who wanders through all worlds as the most sovereign lord.
Able to subdue all classes of dark māras, Able to extinguish all māra-magic,
Constantly encouraging those on the path of virtue, Always assisting and aiding in all wholesome deeds,
Bestowing diligent effort upon those who listen with faith, Acting as a companion throughout all times and days.
Furthermore, they constantly observe the pure and wondrous multitudes, causing them to leave behind the turbid and defiled dharmas of resentment and anger;
through diligent and courageous exertion without leisure, they cause them to escape the poisonous net of Māra’s transgressions;
by distilling the essence of all luminous natures, they personally lead others into the pure Dharma.
Rebuke and punish the evil karma of the various non-Buddhists; do not allow them to harm the gentle assembly.
Bestow glory and joy upon the assembly of light and goodness; cause those of darkness and poison to feel shame and descend to the pure hall of the Dharma.
May the virtuous assembly flourish in its own splendor, free from all enemies.
Manifesting signs of prophecy for vast peace, you can remove fear, terror, and trembling;

you sustain and comfort the assembly of the filial and virtuous. By transmitting excellent faith, you act as a refuge that extinguishes the various poisonous flames of demons and malevolent spirits; thus all falsehoods naturally dissolve.
Fully preparing all robes and armor, may it benefit boys and girls,
and all demonic obstacles and hardships; like the sun rising in full splendor to dissolve dark shadows,
may there be constant joy and tranquility, and may it benefit all that is wholesome and virtuous.
Receiving and guiding us with gifts, you do not decline the labor;
Bringing benefit wherever touched, all the vidyādharas are joyful, expansive, and at ease, adding praise and renown. May this reach all those of the vidyā-kula like yourself;
I pray that the valiant vidyā-messengers will further bestow upon this great assembly the power of firmness.
May you always remain secure and at ease; may you nurture us and increase our meritorious deeds.

You who protect the True Dharma are truly worthy of praise—those known as the Great Powerful Vidyārājas, the lineage of unsurpassed radiance, who constantly bring benefit to the True Dharma everywhere.
May all heavy afflictions and various sufferings be eternally eliminated by the Noble Assembly through the pure Dharma;
may the realms of Māra and his female demons be shattered and dispersed.
May this true Holy Teaching not be obstructed, so that it may eliminate the seeds of all enemies and darkness, establishing the peaceful True Dharma in fearlessness.
Rescue the lambs from the jackals and wolves; Let virtuous men and women find peace therein.
Till away the weeds to purify the fertile field; Constantly reflect upon it so that it may grow.
For the weak, provide them with whips to increase their strength; For the timid, provide them with companions so they have no fear.
O assembly of true beings, you must all make this request: Like an echo, may the māras respond and swiftly come at all times to discipline and purify the assembly.
May those of a joyful nature always be encouraged with strength;
may those who commit evil deeds be made to feel shame; and may those who cultivate wholesome deeds be filled with joy.
The gateway of pure Dharma brings vast tranquility, And further bestows constant, great peace;
I am truly unable to describe it in full detail. How could this praise ever be exhaustive?
All that the Vīra-kula accomplishes is achieved, Its manifold arts and skills are beyond description.
The Venerable One is the one who has subdued anger throughout the kalpas;

all his remaining followers and assistants should be praised at all times. Since he is the ultimate one worthy of praise, we pray that you will deign to hear our petition and, out of great compassion, protect us.
Relying on skillful means, we shall protect ourselves; Our sole aim is to attain peace and be free from enemies.
May this Dharma-gate quickly become vast and secure, Majestic and sublime, without hindrance.
May our path be once again brilliantly illuminated, So that wherever we travel, we may find fearlessness.
O joyful and foremost of all honored ones, from those whose sincere hearts abide in the Dharma,
may each add to their exultation and virtuous deeds; may they surely attain great victory among the noble ones,
and may the vidyā-dhara hosts forgive us, for our compassionate Father has caused them to protect us.
The supreme, noble, and mighty one, having received the command of his compassionate father, protects the True Dharma.
Having become the chief herdsman for the assembly of the enlightened, he naturally wards off all suffering and hardship.
He is the opener of the Dharma and the practitioner of the Way; all who reach this gateway of the Dharma rely upon him.
Those who protect their own happiness abandon worldly glory; they request protection and guard themselves with great effort.
Like a gentle lamb, they diligently gather [their flock]; like a pure seed of light, they naturally defend themselves.
In the field of Dharma, they diligently weed out the thorns so that all sprouts and fruits may flourish and ripen.
Those who have been appointed as envoys and dispatched on the imperial circuit must fully comprehend the Great Sage’s intent;

furthermore, they are fundamentally non-dual with the Dharma-body. May they safely protect this world of the *Sūtra of the Good and Bright Multitude* and the various holy ones established therein, and ensure that the assembly of messengers always provides defense and protection.
Having fulfilled his merit and virtue, this valiant and leaping one— Truly do not slight this true and holy teaching;
he is the chief general, Vajrapāṇi. Always equipped with armor and weapons, he crushes the rebellious factions;
The Great Hero’s pure wind can save his father; He issues all verbal teachings and the constraints of the precepts.
O you who possess merit, courage, and the various vidyās, why do you not diligently attend to what ought to be done?
Do not harbor indolence or change of heart; do not be like those who commit transgressions.
You must be like that capable herdsman who pulls away the lamb to save it from the wolves and tigers.
That Greatly Majestic Holy One, General Who Subdues Māra— this Superior Person constantly remembers the primordial transformation and causes the multitude to adorn themselves naturally;
therefore, he commands the Protectors of the Dharma to bring about vast peace,
subduing all Māras and external paths, while holding the hand of the virtuous multitude with his light.
Exerting diligent valor, always punishing those deluded followers who harm the Dharma,
may you grant joy and the power of compassion to the pure and virtuous assembly who uphold the precepts.
Now I shall briefly describe my names, skills, and arts— those various vidyās that benefit the multitude and the Dharma.
To those among the assembly who assist one another, Who provide equal peace with the Dharma, free from obstacles,
And who rescue and deliver through authoritative means, shattering the ranks of the ignorant— May we always live under the protection of the Father of Clear Wisdom,
Who subdues and overcomes the arrogant Māras, Delighting the pure assembly, and who eternally abides in the secret, great realm of luminosity.
The Sovereign who transcends humans and devas, Dwells with solemn majesty in the Land of Immovability;
Because he takes self-nature as his essence, he opens the gate of wisdom, Causing awakening to arise and revealing the path to nirvana.
He skillfully shows us the ocean of our own life-essence, The ancestral source of light and darkness above and below.
Subtle and wondrous radiance illuminates both within and without; The essence of virtuous karma is gathered and distinguished.
The evil hordes of the Mara-king vie with one another in rage and hatred; Fearing that light will descend and darkness fall, they lack self-mastery.
Alas for the world’s various non-Buddhists! They are unable to discern the luminous source of their own tradition.
Wandering through saṃsāra and hells, one undergoes all manner of calamities; this is truly because one does not seek the authentic path.
I declare to you, O assembly of those with virtuous karma, and to those who can realize these five sciences (*pañcavidyāsthāna*):
You must always remain vigilant and purify the field of the mind; accomplish the father’s legacy without idleness.
Discriminating and simplifying all natures and characteristics, And through the power of awakened clarity,
being bound to this definitive cultivation of the True Dharma— If one can thus swiftly attain liberation,
do not give rise to greed for the desires of the world; Do not be caught by the net of Māra’s household.
Worthy of praise, the Beneficent and Luminous One is the Dharma King; He is able to gather us away from the error of death.
Shining upon both the internal and external, there is nothing he does not illuminate; May we and our kind be equal to the sages.
The tranquil and silent elixir of the immortals is given to the disciples; Those who ingest it immediately attain peace and happiness.
Refining them in the pure Dharma so they may be worthy of praise, Adorning their minds with the five wondrous bodies,
Teaching wisdom and skillful means to your virtuous sons, Causing them all to be fully endowed and truly extraordinary—
O Great Compassionate Father of Radiant Light, By the ancestral power of the virtues you have gathered for your sons.
Striking the bells and beating the drums to announce to all sentient beings: "The time has arrived for this enlightened body to be liberated from its bonds.

Through the power of ultimate analysis that distinguishes light from darkness, as well as all virtuous deeds and their opposing evils, the world, heaven and earth, and the celestial constellations—all shall be dismantled by the Compassionate Honored One.
The māras are imprisoned forever in the dark prison, while the followers of the Buddha leap for joy, returning to the realm of light.
Each resumes their original form in wondrous adornment; donning robes and caps, they attain eternal bliss.
First Stanza: I reverently praise the five great luminous Buddhas, who serve as the impenetrable armor of wisdom.
The wondrous marks of the world’s essence, which sustain all categories of things, the various heavens and earths,
and the life-force of all sentient beings; that which is seen by the eyes and heard as sound by the ears,
which serves as the strength of the bodily joints, and which nourishes all forms and species.
Furthermore, it produces the various words of as many tongues as there are, And likewise produces the various sounds of all melodies;
This is also the vast and brilliant illumination of mind-consciousness, Which can eliminate the darkness of all calamities and sufferings.
It is the wisdom of all benevolent ones, And the eloquence of all who accomplish their tasks.
It can produce a body of exquisite and dignified form; it can bring about all manner of noble and superior benefits;
furthermore, it brings forth the highest nature and all forms of glory and distinction; it also produces all forms of courageous skill and ability.
This is the majestic power of the Sovereign; this is the manifold utility for those who have attained favor.
The excellent medicine for all who are ill, The gentle countenance for all who are contending;
It acts as the ferment for the bodies of all things, And serves as the support that brings about what is to be accomplished.
Furthermore, it is the prosperity and abundance of this world, As well as the various sprouts of plants and trees.
In spring and summer, you soar through the world; every year and every month, you act as the leader.
If there are those with wisdom and merit, why do they not contemplate this great power?
You must always keep these true words in mind, constantly maintaining awe and fear, and never being negligent or disrespectful.
Awakened to the five great luminous Buddhas, Understanding through what causes one comes from the father to this realm,
And knowing that there is no suffering more grievous than this, One skillfully extracts oneself and departs from the demon’s den;
Such a person is called one who possesses eyes, Such a person is called a wise one.
Ceasing all unwholesome karmas, one should return to the ancestral precepts of one's own lineage;
maintaining the fasts and observances with constant vigilance, and through the restraint of mindfulness, always applying healing remedies;
day and night contemplating the true Dharma, one must strive to refine and clarify the five sublime bodies.

Those who wander through the cycle of hellish realms, Those caught in the fires of kalpa or long-term confinement, And those who, though possessing fertile fields of merit, do not recognize the five sciences— They shall thus depart from the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Again, he addressed the brothers Śubhakarma and Jñānakarma: "Apply your minds with focused thought to manifest the wondrous body."
May each become a courageous and wise captain of the ship, To ferry across this drifting child who has wandered to a foreign land.
This is the precious jewel of the Illuminated Honored One; All shall use the boat of the body to cross the ocean.
The diligent physician endures bitter suffering for the sake of sores and wounds; Long have they been filled with sorrow, hoping for rescue and protection.
Please, out of compassion, truly accept [this offering], and immediately according to the number [requested], swiftly return it to the noble owner.

This son, who has wandered for many years, possesses a handsome form, radiant light, and the marks of excellence; quickly send him back to his own native land, a place of peace and happiness, so that he may be swiftly uprooted from the pit of craving.
Seeking precious jewels within the deep and dark ocean of suffering, you hasten to serve the King of Pure Nirvāṇa;
you pull out the cruel thorns and extract the festering sores, washing the bright pearl free from its mire.
You accept the various wondrous offerings presented by Dharma-Śrī, and having adorned yourself with purity, you return to your original Lord.
Counting the flesh and blood—this is precisely what can be received; take as you wish according to your intent.
If you act with falsehood and betray your heart, then when the time of death comes, you will have no path of purification for your own slight transgressions.
Before the King of Equanimity, do not attempt to bend his justice.
The Dharma-nature bestows clarity upon all other Buddhas; for this sake, the Body of Light is ever subject to suffering.
The Buddhas of the past and the Arhats alike established the sublime Dharma within the five sciences (*pañcavidyā*).
Now, the heroic and fierce Mañjuśrī appears before us, manifesting in person.
You who possess wisdom and merit must thoroughly realize the nature of compassion;
diligently apply medical treatments while guarding against what is forbidden. Cause those who suffer from illness to recover, and remain ever firm in your precepts, conduct, and dignified demeanor.
Observe the fasts, perform prostrations, and engage in recitation and praise.
The actions of body, speech, and mind are ever pure; Chanting the words of Dharma continues without interruption.
Furthermore, practicing truthfully with compassion, Being gentle and patient, one purifies the sense faculties.
These are all medicines for the luminous body, By which one is finally freed from painful and distressing afflictions.
A traveler from afar, a guest for a single day, Having been invited with such joy, you have kept this temple-monastery perpetually pure;
Diligently providing robes and provisions, you have emerged from both [sides].
We, your high-ranking disciples, O Honored One of Awakened Wisdom, Are thus able to receive your teachings and explain them with discernment.
Since the Great Sage is the embodiment of virtuous karma, I pray that you descend with compassion so that all may be universally gladdened.
May the Father, out of pity, send down the illuminating messenger, Who can heal the nature of disease, free it from error,
And remove the bonds of all afflictions, Causing the minds of all everywhere to attain happiness.
Nothing hidden remains unmanifest, for all are brought into illumination; All secrets are fully revealed.
These are what are called the two great powers of the two schools: Were it not for those with virtuous seeds, who could bring forth such auspiciousness?
One is lofty and vast, beyond all measure; Both are radiance, where no darkness dwells.
The vidyā-messenger of all Buddhas dwells therein; it is the place where the Vidyārāja is established.
Its radiance is universal and entirely pure; it eternally delights in quiescence and is immovable.
Those who receive its joy are free from affliction; were one to say there is suffering therein, such a thing is impossible.
The Dharma halls of the noble assembly are all solemn and pure;
even within the monasteries of the various Buddhas, one constantly experiences joy amidst radiant light. It is impossible for anyone who has reached that land to suffer from illness;
having attained rebirth there, they will ultimately gather in universal assemblies free from all sorrow.
The noble assembly is sovereign and each dwells in ease; There is forever no cause for flogging, beating, imprisonment, or bondage.
The surroundings are adorned and entirely pure; All evils and impurities were originally non-existent there.
Joy is pervasive, always spacious and tranquil; To say that there is suffering or distress is impossible.
In the world-system Anuttara-prabhāsa, lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are naturally adorned with subtle and wondrous jewels; therein the assembly of noble ones constantly dwells,
and throughout those worlds and lands, the ground of vajra-jewels radiates light down to the very depths.
From beginningless time until now, it is ultimately so: if one says there is shaking or trembling, no such thing exists.
For all those who are among the various sages, they are unstained by ignorance and lust;
having distanced themselves from delusion, craving, and the forms of male and female, how could there be the signs of saṃsāra to urge them on?
The noble assembly is of one mind and in perfect harmony; Though swords may be divided and scattered, they cannot reach them.
Their minds are liberated and unimpeded, And they harbor no desire for sensual pleasures.
The monastic grounds are all solemn and pure; Therein, none harm one another nor engage in discord.
The phenomena of birth, death, destruction, and impermanence—none of these exist within the realm of light;
there are no enemies to invade the borders, nor are there warhorses or garrisons stationed at the outskirts.
Even if the Māra King were to give rise to greedy and lustful thoughts, they would have no share whatsoever within the realm of clarity.
The vajra-jewel ground is most subtle and wondrous; immeasurable, exquisite colors and forms radiate with brilliance.
All the sages dwell therein without hindrance, forever free from dissolution and devoid of sorrow or affliction.
The assembly of holy ones is most extraordinary as they adorn this guest-dwelling; their lights shine upon one another, their bodies radiant and concentrated.
The brilliance of hundreds of thousands of suns and moons is surpassed by the light from the tip of that Sage’s hair;

his inner and outer radiance casts no shadow. His wondrous body constantly shines in ten million ways as he traverses the supreme and renowned Vajra-ground, where not even a hair’s breadth of weight exists.
The renowned garments are all pleasing; they are not produced by human hands.
The robes of the Noble Assembly are exclusively fresh and pure; though worn for a long time, they do not decay nor harbor insects.
All the famous flowers of this world are gathered therein, serving as a metaphor for those subtle, exquisite, and upright features.
Yet their clothing and ornaments are doubled, with marvelous adornments of immeasurable colors;
those temples, pavilions, palaces, and stupas are all accomplished of wondrous jewels, flawless and pure;
food and drink are all sweet and delicious, and the lands are so abundant that there is no famine.
The crown of the Vajra-Flower is ultimately indestructible; once donned, there is no time for it to be removed.
All the holy ones gather together in constant joy, forever free from suffering and never parted.
The flower-crown is exquisitely adorned with lush greenery; its radiance remains ever-fresh and never withers.
Their tongues of flesh desire to praise [you], yet it is beyond the power of thought; Your wondrous form is inexhaustible and never fades.
The bodies of the Noble Assembly are light and ever-pure; Hands, feet, and all limbs are free from obstruction.
Since you do not create the karma of conditioned birth and death, How could one say that you experience exhaustion?
Those noble ones possess pure and empty bodies that are ever-blissful; their vajra-natures are without sleep.
Since they have neither dreams nor delusions, how could it be said that they experience fear?
The assembly of noble ones is eternally luminous and endowed with wondrous wisdom; forgetfulness and indeterminate states have never existed within them from the beginning.
The various phenomena of boundless worlds are all seen as if reflected in a clear mirror;
the minds of all the sages are entirely true, for deceit, falsehood, and pretension have never existed therein.
Since their actions of body, speech, and mind are eternally pure, how could it be said that they speak words of falsehood?
The world is filled with all manner of precious jewels; there is not a single thing that cannot be praised.

The monasteries are vast and spacious, lacking nothing at all. How could one say there is poverty, suffering from the heat of hunger, or any such hardships? In this realm of light and eternal bliss, none of these exist.
Forever free from the afflictions of hunger and thirst, there are no waters of salt or bitterness, nor rivers, seas, or springs.
The life-sustaining waters are limpid, fragrant, and sublime;
upon entering them, one neither drifts nor sinks, and no violent floods come to cause depletion or harm.
The Noble Ones always dwell in peace and happiness; their land is worthy of praise and free from mutual disparagement or resentment.
There is no suffering born of association with the disliked, for such things are fundamentally absent there. They do not praise one another's faces nor do they slander each other;
instead, they leap with compassion, feeling deep pity for one another. Envy, jealousy, and all manner of evils are fundamentally absent there.
Your gait is swift and rapid, surpassing the wind; it is impossible for your four limbs to be paralyzed or sluggish.

Your supernormal powers move as fast as lightning; manifesting throughout the ten directions without obstruction, your wondrous and extraordinary form is truly difficult to describe. No calamities or illnesses can harm you.
The various calamities of oppression and narrow straits, All fearsome demonic affairs, battles, mutual harm, and killing— Within the realm of light none of these exist;
this world is eternally peaceful and free from terror. The land is majestic and pure, with nothing that can cause distress.
The ground of vajra-jewels is boundless; it is impossible for it ever to be destroyed.
There, rows of jewel trees stand in perfect order; their precious fruits are always produced, never withering or decaying.
They are uniform in size, free from insects, and naturally lush and verdant.
Bitter, poisonous, sour, astringent, and dark-rotten; The fragrant and delicious jewel-fruits are not like this.
Neither hollow within nor solid without, They are radiant throughout, with the taste of nectar.
From the roots and trunk to the branches and leaves of the jewel-tree, Throughout the entire body from top to bottom, all is nectar.
Fragrant scents pervade the world, And precious flowers reflect one another, ever crimson and white.
The gardens and groves of that land are vast, majestic, and pure; How could it be otherwise that wondrous fragrances surround every orchard?
As for the presence of rubble, thorns, or any foul weeds— To say such things exist would be impossible.
That vajra ground is ever radiant, Internally and externally reflecting, such that there is nothing unseen;
The jewel-ground is layered upon layers, with infinite lands, Piercing through every interval, all clearly manifest.
Auspicious fragrances swirl throughout the world, A pure and unadulterated ocean of life and nature.
Encompassing and pervading all without obstruction, The assembly of sages wanders therein; their sublime fragrance is supreme.
The nature of space is thus, without change, A cloud of subtle light, shadowless and unimpeded.
Serene, pure, and free from dust or veil, It extends equally throughout all worlds.
In that realm, there are billions of kinds of jewel mountains, From which hundreds of thousands of varieties of incense smoke surge forth.
The inner and outer bodies of light are pure and clear; Amrita fills them to the very limits, without bound.
Fountains and clear streams flow without interruption; The true taste of amrita is free from any bitterness.
The noble assembly is fully satiated, lacking for nothing; it is impossible for them to suffer thirst or want.
A wondrous breeze wafts and drifts, bringing delight to all; harmonious and refreshing, it pervades the ten directions.
It gently brushes against the jeweled towers and pavilions, while the precious bells and chimes constantly ring out in resonance.
The wondrous fire of radiance is beyond compare; its exquisite color is cool and perpetually brilliant, shining with constant splendor, eternal and neither arising nor ceasing.
This extraordinary luster is truly difficult to liken to anything else;
the essence of this fire is pure and void, free from toxic heat, so that when one enters it through touch, one is not burned or cooked.
There are no ashes or soot remaining; if one says it was burned away, that is impossible.
The halls and palaces there are all not made by human hands;
they are firm and formed spontaneously without effort, for such is their natural law. If one says they were constructed through labor, that is impossible.
Those who emerge from the precious ground all possess seeing, hearing, and cognitive awareness;
they behold the Unsurpassed King of Nirvāṇa and extol and sing the praises of the Great Sage’s majesty.
In that place, shadows have never existed from the very beginning, and all internal and external luminosity is peerless.
All the physical marks of his body are most wondrous; upon the jeweled ground they are ever verdant.
The forms of the assembly of sages are most extraordinary; their lofty, vast, and majestic countenances are truly inconceivable.
Reaching down to the base of the jeweled ground without limit, there is no way to know their measure.
That noble and wondrous form is worthy of deep veneration; It is fundamentally free from illness and calamity, possessing power that is ever-secure and devoid of decay.
To say it is without impairment and its body is eternally robust— Were it not for a Great Sage who knows the measure of the body, what ordinary person could calculate or describe it?
The adamantine body is inconceivable; its large and small forms are distinguished only by the sages.
The physical marks of the assembly of sages are most subtle and wondrous;
they emit great radiance throughout boundless realms, from the beginningless past through the present until the ultimate end. To say that this body perishes is impossible.
Among all classes of beings—humans, devas, sages, and ordinary folk—none possess a tongue of flesh capable of praising them;
the true nature and characteristics of those Buddhas are truly inconceivable. The precious vajra-ground is likewise so;
the assembly of sages always delights therein without ever wearying, cherishing its sublime splendor with ultimate joy.
The physical marks are subtle and ever-attendant; their inner and outer adornments are truly difficult to describe.
The radiance of the noble assembly is most extraordinary, uninterrupted and mutually illuminating one another.
Those sages are of one mind and in perfect harmony; were one to analyze them into parts, they would fundamentally not exist.
The sublime countenances and wondrous marks of all the Sages, Abiding within the jeweled palaces and pavilions of the monasteries,
Their every thought, intention, and mental perception Universally observe and examine all things without error.
Within this realm of radiant light, all the Sages Have bodies that are supple and agile, free from weariness or heaviness.
With wondrous forms, they travel through all lands at will; Their mental manifestations are entirely identical to those of the holy assembly.
With one mind, they are ever joyful; They proclaim subtle and wondrous sounds without ceasing.
Praising and extolling them without weariness, They universally laud the Sage’s virtuous deeds and majestic power.
The wondrous sounds of their hymns are all delightful; their voices are pure, beautiful, and profoundly serene.
From top to bottom, they resonate in unison with sublime echoes that pervade the monastery without ceasing.
Their voices flow forth with extraordinary excellence, singing and praising one another’s wondrous virtues.
The bliss of all the noble ones is ultimate; eternally abiding and ever-peaceful, it is free from exhaustion.
This radiant jewel-ground is boundless; there is no place where one might seek its edge or shore.
It is fundamentally without confinement or obstruction, such that each may roam at ease wherever they choose.
The noble assembly is of one mind and in perfect harmony; From the beginning, there is no division, nor contention for fame or profit.
In universal equality, all are fully present; They dwell together in the vast and expansive monastery.
The monastery is pure and wondrously adorned; From the beginning, it is free from fear and obstacles.
The streets and alleys are vast and magnificently adorned; wherever one wanders at will, all is universally auspicious.

All the various māras and hungry ghosts—with their hideous faces and misshapen bodies—whether speaking of existence or non-existence from the beginningless past through the present and into the future, such claims have no basis in truth.

Chickens, dogs, pigs, [oxen], and other such species—within the realm of Nirvana, these five classes of birds and beasts and their various sounds do not exist at all. If one were to say they exist there, it would be impossible;
likewise, all shadows and dust are entirely absent from the world of Ultimate Bliss.
All the noble monasteries are entirely pure; there is no place for darkness, as radiant light fills all things.
Life reaches its ultimate fulfillment in eternal peace, and precious joy is fundamentally uninterrupted. Their compassionate hearts are true and ever-expansive.
Always delighting in joy without ceasing, with body and mind refreshed within precious fragrances, they do not calculate years, months, seasons, or days;
how could they worry about the end of life or the three periods?
All sages are without birth or extinction; the demon of impermanence cannot harm them.
Not practicing sexual desire, one is free from the defilement of conception;
how could it be said that there is delusion or craving that destroys the male and female bodies?
In the world of Ultimate Bliss, where birth and death are impermanent, such fruits of lust do not exist at all; that place is pure and free from calamities.
Within the realm of radiant light, the noble ones abide; Free from gestation in a womb, they neither gather nor disperse.
Throughout all lands there is peace and no terror; From the very beginning, there has been no fear or chaos.
All arises from the wondrous speech of the living word; The manifestations of the noble assembly appear through these conditions.
Each birth and transformation is fundamentally adorned; each is similar, with no distinction seen.
The lands are all comparable in size, and the monasteries and hermitages for peaceful dwelling are likewise without difference.
Each emits immeasurable light, and their lifespans reach their ultimate end without being recorded in years.
All its boundaries are eternally tranquil; its nature and characteristics are equal, with no difference in the ground.
The three constants mutually stabilize one another in great brilliance; that which they call "existence" is fundamentally darkness and non-existent—this is what is called the Land of Constant Joy.
The luminosity of all Buddhas serves as the causal condition for its original manifestation.
There shall be no three calamities nor the eight difficulties; birth, old age, sickness, and death shall not pass one another.
This is the Great Power of Suchness, which Mañjuśrī clearly proclaims, able to reveal the true path of the conditions for birth. May the assembly of sages gather everywhere and attain this.
This is to be used during the first ten-day period of fasting and silence while making vows.
One should praise Mañjughoṣa, the King of Wisdom, as well as the five pure vidyārājas,
all the vidyādharas, and those who protect the true Dharma.
To all the compassionate fathers of the past, To all the Mūṣakas of the past, To all the Vṛddhatāns of the past, And to all the masters of the Dharma-halls of the past—
Whether men or women, endowed with precepts and liberated— May they all attain peace and happiness, and be universally praised.
"May all deceased listeners who have sunk into the cycle of rebirth / Be rescued by the assembly of sages and reach the further shore.

All you laymen and laywomen who offer with faith, And all those who have formed a karmic connection with this True Dharma,
Relying upon the gate of liberation of the Resplendent Honored One, I universally pray that you may leave behind all sufferings of birth and death.
May the merit created today be gathered in, And may the Resplendent Ones receive it all and lead you away.
May all celestial seers, virtuous deities, and the like, Dwell in peace and dispel all calamities.

Musha constantly aspires to travel without hindrance; Duodan dwells in peace wherever he goes.
The presiding master of the Dharma Hall increases his joy; The preceptor-monks augment their power of merit.
The pure young maidens are urged to diligence; All you listening disciples, may you attain great awakening.
The assembly of noble ones protects and guards this Dharma hall; we are always at ease and free from anxiety.

(Recite these three lines and perform three prostrations. For those standing, once the recitation is finished, join with the preceding verse for the conclusion; then the entire assembly joins together.
In unison they said: "We are the foremost among men;

When we had finished the preceding ritual, the assembly fell silent; the Venerable One then recited the *Āvartanī-gāthā*, followed by:
"The wondrous body of radiance binds;
may the wondrous body of radiance swiftly bring liberation, so that the transgressions of this donor may be extinguished."
May all teachers, preceptors, and disciples alike share in this merit;
may they honor the True Dharma and attain unimpeded circulation of it. May it be thus, to the ultimate and final degree.
This verse concludes the praise of the Honored One of Radiance; it is used at the end to seal the vow.
Great Lord of Reality, King of Twelve Radiances,
[ruler of] lands as numerous as the atoms within the World of Myriad Wonders, Ever-Living Sublime Space,
Maker of Light upon the Ground Worthy of Praise, Honored Buddha Mañjuśrī, who has abandoned all transgressions.
Whether obstructed or unobstructed, whether at times following one’s own intention or the intentions of others—
regarding all such unwholesome actions of body, speech, and thought— we members of this virtuous assembly and all who listen,
having requested forgiveness for our transgressions, shall each act according to our original vows.
This verse concludes the praise of the Sun after the eulogy; it is used for the final dedication of merit.
I praise the subtle and great radiance, The most supreme and peerless light in the world, Extraordinary and pervasive throughout the ten directions, Bringing joy during all twelve periods of the day.
O Greatly Powerful, Praised, and Compassionate Mother; O Twelve Pure Vital Winds, the Swift and Leaping, the Fierce and Fierce;
O Five Gatherers, the Radiant One, and the countless hosts of luminous beings—each of you, out of your compassionate power, please look upon us with mercy!
We entreat you to rescue all those of luminous nature who are in universal distress.
"May we escape the great waves of the fire-ocean; may the assembly together fulfill their ultimate vows.
This verse concludes the praise of Vairocana and is used for the final dedication of merit.
Praised and renowned, Sulūśara, the noble and perfect Great Minister, with the vajra-marked pillar,
upholding the world; pervading all with his own wondrous body and by his own great power, he benefits those who acknowledge him as their own.
I, Gusi Chongzi, now offer this humble petition; we are unable to praise you fully, yet we pray that you will graciously accept it.
May you protect and assist the virtuous multitude always according to their wishes.
This verse concludes the praise for Yishu; it is used as the final prayer of dedication.
Praising pure and wondrous wisdom, the one of *iṣu*-like radiance manifests as celestial youths and maidens;
with a vast mind and prior tranquility of intent,
he is the nature of all *tathatā*, the reawakened essence of all that is subtle and exquisite.
For the sick, you act as the King of Physicians; for those in suffering, you bring them joy through your renown.
You are the gatherer of the five clear messengers and the master of the seven ships.
Mañjuśrī, Compassionate Father and Radiant One, may you forgive all my transgressions, and may the entire assembly be safe and well, just as they have wished.
This verse concludes the praise of the Buddha Maṇikūṭa; it is used for the final dedication of merit.
I praise and extol the precious and vast Lord of Truth, King of Supreme Radiance, together with his noble assembly in the world of Constant Illumination.
Mañjuśrī, Dharma King; Mañjughoṣa, Lord of Wisdom.
From beyond the three realms, you have come into the midst of birth and death. You have awakened our nature as the Great Physician King;
acting as the one who brings definitive peace, you open the spring of nectar.
Planting the tree of livelihood, you rescue the multitude of your fellow countrymen;
gathering the children of light among the gentle flock, you act as their shepherd.
You cause the field of merit to flourish with abundant sprouts and fruit, and you serve as the guardian of the pure Dharma.
Homage to the majestic and powerful one, whose deep kindness inspires shame and gratitude.
Before the Most Honored One and the assembly of radiant beings, we deeply receive this great grace.
We offer our profound thanks for this vast bounty, which truly belongs to us; it has removed our great calamities and brought us immense joy.
We now, before all the Noble Ones, with sincere hearts and earnest devotion,
repent for all our negligence regarding the salt-seal of the supreme method received from the Buddha Maṅgali, which we have vowed to maintain day and night.
We dare not be negligent or disrespectful; now, we shall practice with resolute determination in this single Pure Name, until we ultimately attain victory.
Just as in our original vows—let this verse be used daily by all to conclude their prayers.
I pay homage and offer praise; I constantly and extensively extol this present day.
For those who possess the nature of bliss among all that exists, this is the most excellent of times; now, enter the fragrant waters.
Washing away all defilements and impurities, one should abide in accordance with the Dharma;
praising those of great majestic form, they pervade the pure Dharma.
Thus, the Buddha of the Yi-śu clan is able to revive all seeds of goodness.
Praise to the True Lord, the mighty Mañjuśrī,
who can revitalize the essence of pure phenomena and rescue all luminous natures.
With eyes of compassion, please look upon this assembly of the pure.
In such a most minute assembly, in such a most minute place,
I pray only that you may protect and shield me; constantly apply your power and exhortation,
so that the obstructed body may become unobstructed, and you may always bestow your grace upon both the internal and external.
We, the sons of the pure Dharma, all the steadfast maidens,
and those who listen— may we ultimately fulfill our vows.
(This verse is to be recited every day when reaching the point of confession with the listeners.)

Boundless assembly of noble ones, immovable and unshakeable; The vajra-jewel ground facing the palaces of the sun and moon;

When the day of impermanence arrives—
Having escaped this loathsome physical body,
one is surrounded by all the Buddhas and noble sages; a jeweled boat,
established through one's own wholesome karma, comes to welcome them.
He proceeded until he stood before King Samatā,
where he received three great and supreme gifts:
namely, a flower crown, necklaces, ten thousand kinds of exquisite garments, and various ornaments to wear.

furthermore, from the presence of King Samatā,
they were surrounded before and behind by banners, flowers, and precious canopies.
The assembly of sages sings praises as they enter the realm of Rocana.
Within that realm, the roads are level and straight;
their voices, resonant like the Brahma-sound, pervade and cover all around.
From there, they proceed as far as the palaces of the sun and moon,
where they each enjoy inexhaustible bliss and receive endless praise from the six Great Compassionate Fathers and their other retinues.
Furthermore, they are further led across to the other shore,
whereupon they enter the eternally luminous world of nirvāṇa,
where they constantly experience happiness through their own virtuous karma.
May the entire assembly be of one mind, just as in the above vows.

The lower vow consists of five grades, from the *Mingqun* (Clarifying the Multitudes) up to the "Worthy and Sages of the Ten Directions," which are intended to be sacred words that are inexhaustible, whereas ordinary consciousness has its limits. The Sanskrit original contains three thousand articles, of which more than twenty paths have been translated. Furthermore, regarding the verses for recitation (*geya*) and hymns (*stotra*), it is wished that they all be composed according to the four locations [of the musical modes]. As for those translations by Daoming, they strictly follow the Sanskrit originals; thus, if there are students who wish to practice them, they should do so accordingly.

The lofty brilliance of the sun and moon;
